questions.text:
QUESTION ONE: DC AND CAPACITORS

Ana's electric bicycle battery has an EMF of 48.0 V and an internal resistance of 0.120 ohm.

Explain the meaning of the term EMF.
questions.expectedAnswer: EMF is the voltage across the terminals of the battery when no current flows. It represents the total energy per coulomb supplied by the battery.

questions.text:
Ana observes the voltmeter reading while opening and closing the switch.

Explain why the readings are the same or different. Values and calculations are not required.
questions.expectedAnswer: Switch open: voltmeter reads 48.0 V (no current, no voltage drop across internal resistance). Switch closed: voltmeter reads less than 48.0 V because current flows through the internal resistance, causing a voltage drop.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE correct statement. Merit: Complete answer.

questions.text:
After long use the internal resistance increases to 0.800 ohm. The discharged battery is charged by a 60.0 V DC supply with a 14.0 ohm resistor in series.

Calculate the terminal voltage across the bicycle battery.

Begin by calculating the circuit current.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One step correct. Merit: I correct. Excellence: V_terminal = 48.6 V.

questions.text:
Ana connects a 48.0 V DC supply to a 0.200 F capacitor, two indicator lights, and a resistor, as shown. The resistor and lights each have resistance 8.00 ohm.

Give an in-depth explanation of what Ana would observe by comparing the brightness of lights A and B:

- as soon as the switch is closed
- ten seconds after the switch is closed.
questions.expectedAnswer: Initially: Light A glows brightly as capacitor charges (large current flows through it). Light B also glows but less brightly as it shares voltage with the resistor. After 10 seconds: capacitor is fully charged, no more current flows through A, so A goes dark. B continues to glow as current still flows through the resistor branch.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE correct observation. Merit: TWO correct observations. Excellence: ALL correct with explanations.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION

Liam is experimenting with coils and magnets.

Liam measures an average EMF of 180 microV induced in a coil when the current changes from 8.00 A to 5.00 A in 0.500 s.

Calculate the self-inductance of the coil.

The coil has 30 turns and an area of 2.00 cm2 (2.00 x 10^-4 m2). It is inserted into a magnetic field of flux density 1.50 Wb m-2, perpendicular to the field lines. It takes 0.250 s.

Calculate the EMF induced in the coil.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One sub-calculation correct. Merit: V = 0.0360 V.

questions.text:
Liam drops a bar magnet through a metal ring.

Explain why its acceleration will not be equal to g = 9.81 m s-2.

Include ideas about when the magnet enters and leaves the ring.
questions.expectedAnswer: As the magnet enters: changing flux induces a current in the ring (Faraday's law). By Lenz's law, this current creates a magnetic field opposing the change, repelling the magnet and reducing its acceleration below g. As the magnet leaves: the flux is decreasing, so the induced current creates a field that attracts the magnet, again opposing the motion and reducing acceleration.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE correct statement. Merit: Explains opposition to motion. Excellence: Explains both entering and leaving.

questions.text:
Liam connects a 0.500 H inductor and a lamp of resistance 2.50 ohm in series to a battery. The lamp takes some time to reach full brightness.

Calculate the current through the lamp after 0.500 seconds.

Begin by calculating the time constant.
questions.expectedAnswer: I_max = V/R = 48.0/2.50 = 19.2 A (using 48V supply). Actually, let me use a generic approach: tau = L/R = 0.500/2.50 = 0.200 s. 0.500 s = 2 tau. I = I_max(1 - 1/e^2) = I_max x 0.8647. If V = 13.5 V: I_max = 12.0/2.50 = 4.80 A. I = 4.80 x 0.8647 = 4.15 A.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: tau = 0.200 s OR I_max. Merit: Correct sub-calculations. Excellence: Correct I.

questions.text:
QUESTION THREE: AC

Sophie connects a 80.0 mH inductor with a soft iron core and a 50.0 ohm bulb in series to a 120 V_rms, 50.0 Hz supply.

Calculate the peak voltage.

Calculate the phase difference between the supply voltage and the circuit current, and state which leads.

Begin by showing that the reactance of the inductor is 25.1 ohm.
questions.expectedAnswer: X_L = 2 pi f L = 2 pi x 50.0 x 0.0800 = 25.13 ohm. tan theta = X_L/R = 25.13/50.0 = 0.5027. theta = 26.7 degrees. Source voltage leads current.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: X_L = 25.1 ohm. Merit: theta calculated. Excellence: Complete with phasor diagram.

questions.text:
The inductor has a soft iron core.

Explain what Sophie would observe in the brightness of the lamp when she slowly removes the iron core.
questions.expectedAnswer: Removing the core decreases L, which decreases X_L, which decreases Z, which increases I, which increases power in the bulb. The lamp becomes brighter.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE step correct. Merit: Chain of reasoning. Excellence: Full explanation with power.

questions.text:
Sophie adds a capacitor to achieve resonance. The reactance of the inductor is 25.1 ohm.

Explain why the capacitor reactance needs to be 25.1 ohm.

Begin by describing what happens at resonance.
questions.expectedAnswer: At resonance, X_L = X_C. The voltages across the inductor and capacitor are equal and opposite, so they cancel. Z = R (minimum impedance), so I is maximum. Therefore X_C must equal 25.1 ohm.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One correct statement. Merit: Two correct. Excellence: Full explanation.
